extracted.intended_audience: Attorneys/practitioners admitted to practice before the USPTO (trademark and non-patent practitioners), USPTO OED staff, and respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards for imposing reciprocal discipline (indefinite suspension) by the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, including notice, response opportunity, publication, interstate notice, duties after discipline, and conditions for reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by a state's disciplinary authority by filing a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 and issuing a Notice and Order to the respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order provides the respondent an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline based on one or more reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1). In this case the Notice and Order was sent by certified mail and delivered; respondent's failure to file a response resulted in a determination that there was no genuine issue of material fact and that identical discipline was appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's opportunity and grounds to oppose reciprocal discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent may oppose imposition of identical reciprocal discipline by filing a timely response arguing one or more specified reasons set out in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice grants a 40-day period to submit such opposition; failure to respond may be treated as creating no genuine issue of material fact and permit imposition of reciprocal discipline. (The specific statutory/regulatory reasons to oppose are contained in § 11.24(d)(1).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) as basis for USPTO suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) (predicated upon being indefinitely suspended from practice of law by a duly constituted state authority) supports indefinite suspension from practice before the USPTO in trademark and other non-patent matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order expressly states respondent was indefinitely suspended from USPTO practice for violating § 11.804(h), based on the Maryland suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement procedure under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent suspended by the USPTO may apply for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement may be sought upon providing notice that the respondent has been reinstated in the state of admission, or after five years from the date of the Final Order, whichever is earlier (as stated in this particular Order).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties after discipline per 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: A disciplined practitioner must comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 following imposition of public discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires respondent to comply with the duties listed in § 11.58 (the document does not list them here but directs compliance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies and courts pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice, pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, of the public discipline and the reasons for it to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the states where the respondent is admitted, to courts where the respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This Order directs the OED Director to provide such notice to the relevant state agencies, courts, and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of suspension notice in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a notice of suspension in the USPTO Official Gazette describing the respondent, the practice areas affected, the regulatory basis for suspension, and the underlying state order and rules violated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order includes a sample 'NOTICE OF SUSPENSION' text detailing the respondent, affected practice (trademark and non-patent matters), violated regulation (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)), the underlying Maryland Court of Appeals order, and the specific Maryland Lawyers' Rules of Professional Conduct found to have been violated.

rubrics_metrics.name: State disciplinary findings and applicable professional conduct rules
rubrics_metrics.description: State findings of professional misconduct (here, the Maryland Court of Appeals order) that identify violations of specific state professional conduct rules can predicate USPTO reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites the Maryland findings that respondent violated Maryland Lawyers' Rules of Professional Conduct rules 1.2 (Scope of Representation); 1.4 (Communication); 1.6 (Confidentiality of Information); 1.9 (Duties to Former Clients); 1.16(d) (Termination of Representation); 3.1 (Meritorious Claims and Contentions); 4.4 (Respect for Rights of Third Persons); and 8.4 (Misconduct). Those state-rule violations were the predicate for the USPTO action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority for USPTO disciplinary action (35 U.S.C. § 32)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO takes disciplinary action pursuant to statutory authority, specifically 35 U.S.C. § 32, in conjunction with its regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states the action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 and notes that disciplinary decisions are publicly available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of disciplinary decisions (FOIA Reading Room)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions are available for public review at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's FOIA Reading Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order gives the URL (http://e-foia.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp) where disciplinary decisions are posted for public access.
